title: The two Cartier divisor classes agree and pull back
statement:
Fix the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$ and twists of [def-pur-conventions], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Use the general effective-Cartier-divisor construction in the second paragraph of [lem-pur-divisor-class], which uses $\mathcal O_T(D)$ with its specified canonical trivialization on $W=T\setminus D$, without requiring $D\to T$ to be smooth. It gives $\operatorname{cl}(D)\in H^2_D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1))$ [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Then, under the identification $H^2_D(T,A(1))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*A_D,A_T(1)[2])$ of [lem-pur-supported-hom], $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ is the morphism $c_D$ of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map].

Here the named $c_D$ has the explicit normalization of its source's relative-torsor construction: put $N=\ell^n$, $R=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$, take the relative Kummer boundary of the frame torsor of $(\mathcal O_T(D),s_D|_W)$, realize it as $b_D:i_*R_D\to\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}[2]$ via [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], apply derived scalar extension $-\otimes_R^L A$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], and then the canonical etale-to-pro-etale and supported-source comparisons and the roots-projection target identification of [def-pur-frame-class]. This specifies the constructed morphism referred to by that name.

Consequently, for every morphism $h:T'\to T$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes such that $D'=T'\times_TD$ is an effective Cartier divisor of $T'$, the supported pullback of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] satisfies
$$h^*\operatorname{cl}(D)=\operatorname{cl}(D')\quad\text{in }H^2_{D'}(T',A(1)).$$
No smoothness of $T$, $D$, $T'$ or $D'$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $W=T\setminus D$. The general construction explicitly stated in [lem-pur-divisor-class] applies to this Cartier divisor; the smooth-subfamily hypotheses belong to its first clause. Write $L=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. If $\mathcal I_D=(f_a)$, let $e_a$ be the basis dual to $f_a$; the canonical section is $s_D=f_ae_a$. On overlaps $e_b=(f_a/f_b)e_a$, whence $f_be_b=f_ae_a$. On $W$ this is a frame. Thus both recipes start with the same global line bundle and specified frame, including the trivialization data. By [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor] its frame sheaf $P_D$ is a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor. By [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] the pair $(P_D,s_D|_W)$ has a specified class $\alpha_D\in H^1(T,W;\mathbf G_m)$.

proof.text: Regard $\mu_N^{\mathrm{et}}$ as an $R_T$-module sheaf. The derived module-to-abelian comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-underlying-comparison], for the identity and for $W\to T$, commutes with restriction. It consequently identifies their relative cones: its maps on the two derived section complexes are isomorphisms, and therefore so is its cone map, as the cone long exact sequences show. Under [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] let $b_D:i_*R_D\to\mu_N^{\mathrm{et}}[2]$ represent $\beta_D$. The relative-to-supported identification of [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone] uses the kernel inclusion $k\mapsto(k,0)$ in the signed restriction cone. Use this same restriction cone for support-Hom. Thus this fixes the relative lift and its sign before any coefficient change; no choice of a lift from ordinary first Chern classes occurs.

source.place: Third paragraph: supported R-module realization of the relative Kummer boundary

proof.text:
A closed immersion is finite: on an affine open it is induced by a quotient ring, generated as a module by $1$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], its etale direct image is exact. This also holds for module sheaves, since forgetting to abelian sheaves computes kernels and cokernels. Applying an exact functor to a resolution computes its derived functor, so $Ri_*A_D=i_*A_D$. Let $L_A=-\otimes_R^L A$ and let $\eta$ be its unit against exact scalar restriction, normalized as in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Put $P_R=i_*R_D$. The scalar-extension clause of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] supplies the canonical identifications $L_AP_R=i_*A_D$ and $L_A\mu_N^{\mathrm{et}}=B=\mu_N^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_R A$. The root sheaf is flat by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] with coefficient ring $R$, and is K-flat in degree zero by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], so $B$ is in degree zero. Denote the extended morphism $L_A b_D$ by $b_{D,A}$. Naturality of the unit gives
$$\operatorname{Res}(L_A b_D)\circ\eta_{P_R}=\eta_{\mu_N^{\mathrm{et}}}[2]\circ b_D.$$
In the supported-Hom realization of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], this says that $b_{D,A}$ represents $u_*\beta_D$, where $u(v)=v\otimes1$. Explicitly the unit at the supported source sends its local constant generator $1$ to $1_A$, and at the target sends a root $v$ to $v\otimes1$. Evaluating a supported Hom cocycle at the generator therefore identifies the displayed square with the coefficient map on the kernel of restriction, and hence on its derived restriction cone. This uses the normalized adjunction and does not require $A$ to be flat over $R$.

u^{-1}u=t$ by substituting $a=1$. This is the projection-induced identification with the specified twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. proof.text: The right side in step 5 is precisely the explicit recipe for the named $c_D$ fixed in the statement: the relative torsor Kummer boundary is realized over $R$, extended to $A$, and then carried through the supported-source and roots-projection comparisons. The recipes have the identical $\alpha_D$, $\beta_D$, coefficient unit $v\mapsto v\otimes1$, and source comparison. Thus steps 2 and 5 give $\chi_{T,D}(\operatorname{cl}(D))=c_D$. This is a substitution of the constructed map's explicit normalization. The first-Chern-class and base-change properties asserted by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] alone are not being used to characterize it uniquely.

source.place: Explicit construction of c_D, expanded as a convention in the item statement

proof.text:
For the given $h:T'\to T$, both $D$ and $D'$ are Cartier, so [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] gives $h^{-1}c_D=c_{D'}$ under its canonical source and twist comparisons. The twist has the bounded-below etale-origin witness $B[0]$ of step 5. The pro-etale assertion of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] therefore gives
$$\chi_{T',D'}(h^*\operatorname{cl}(D))=h^{-1}(\chi_{T,D}(\operatorname{cl}(D)))=h^{-1}c_D=c_{D'}=\chi_{T',D'}(\operatorname{cl}(D')).$$
Here pullback of the supported morphism includes precomposition with the inverse supported-constant comparison. The pullback in [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] is the canonical supported pullback on both sites, compatible with localization and the site comparison, hence is the map in this formula. Finally $\chi_{T',D'}$ is injective by [lem-pur-supported-hom], giving the required equality. All inputs use Cartier divisors and the invertible exponent killing $A$; none requires these schemes or divisors to be smooth.
